verdict.rationale: Gusto Embedded documents registrable webhooks. Developers create subscriptions for chosen subscription_types, verify them with a verification_token, and check HMAC signatures, and a webhooks health-check endpoint exists. Of the payroll lifecycle events, only payroll.paid (payroll processed) is explicitly documented. missing for 10: documented employee-onboarded event, documented payment-failed event, full event catalog, independent/hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to payroll lifecycle events (payroll processed, employee onboarded, payment failed) via webhooks to drive downstream automations

citations.quote: Create a webhook subscription to receive events of the specified subscription_types whenever there is a state change.
Gusto will publish this webhook event when payroll credits have been generated and payments will be made.
This `verify` endpoint needs to be called with `verification_token` before webhook events can be sent to the registered webhook URL.
Gusto computes a hash message authentication code (HMAC) of the event payload using the verification_token
We recommend that you integrate with Gusto's webhooks infrastructure so that your application can perform subsequent business logic after it receives a webhook event.
